local-infrastructure: Docker-based local .NET dev/test stack: SQL Server 2025 Developer, PostgreSQL 16, Azure Service Bus Emulator; license-free.

Files: `.env.example` (copy to `.env`), `.gitignore`, `docker-compose.yml`, `stack.ps1`, `README.md`, `Config.example.json` (copy to `servicebus/Config.json`), `servicebus/monitor/Program.cs`, `ServiceBusMonitor.csproj`.

Requires Docker Compose v2+, PowerShell 5.1+, .NET 8; Docker Engine, Rancher Desktop, or Podman (no Docker Desktop required).

Services: `local-mssql` port 1433 (`sqlcmd` healthcheck); `local-postgres` port 5432 (`pg_isready`); `local-servicebus-sql` internal/no exposed port (`sqlcmd`); `local-servicebus` ports 5672 AMQP, 5300 management/health. Service Bus health is host-probed by `stack.ps1` via HTTP GET `/health` (image has no shell); depends on healthy `servicebus-sql`. All services use `restart: unless-stopped` and named persistent volumes.

Commands:
.\stack.ps1 start
.\stack.ps1 stop
.\stack.ps1 restart
.\stack.ps1 nuke
.\stack.ps1 status
.\stack.ps1 logs [service]
.\stack.ps1 pull
.\stack.ps1 monitor
docker compose up -d
docker compose down
docker compose down -v
cd servicebus/monitor

Copy `.env.example` → `.env`; set placeholders. Variables: `MSSQL_SA_PASSWORD` (min 8 chars, upper/lower/digit/special), `MSSQL_PORT` (1433), `POSTGRES_USER`, `POSTGRES_PASSWORD`, `POSTGRES_DB`, `POSTGRES_PORT` (5432), `SERVICEBUS_SQL_PASSWORD` (same complexity), `SERVICEBUS_PORT` (5672), `SERVICEBUS_MGMT_PORT` (5300).

Connection strings:
Server=localhost,1433;User Id=sa;Password=<MSSQL_SA_PASSWORD>;TrustServerCertificate=True;
Host=localhost;Port=5432;Database=<POSTGRES_DB>;Username=<POSTGRES_USER>;Password=<POSTGRES_PASSWORD>;
Endpoint=sb://localhost;SharedAccessKeyName=RootManageSharedAccessKey;SharedAccessKey=SAS_KEY_VALUE;UseDevelopmentEmulator=true;
`SAS_KEY_VALUE` can be any non-empty string; requires `Azure.Messaging.ServiceBus` ≥ 7.18.0.

PowerShell: `#Requires -Version 5.1`; `Set-StrictMode -Version Latest`; `$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'`. ANSI fallback; Unicode TUI. Validate Docker daemon and `.env` before operations. Functions: `Invoke-<Action>`, `Get-<Property>`, `Assert-<Condition>`, `Wait-<State>`, `Show-<View>`. Preserve TUI consistency. .NET 8, implicit usings, nullable enabled; modern C#, retry/backoff 1–30 s; cap collections at 1000.

Compose: Every service must have a `healthcheck` block. Secrets from `.env` via `${VAR:-default}`; named volumes for persistent data; 2-space indentation; follow Azure Service Bus Emulator schema. `Config.example.json` is safe-to-commit template; `Config.json` is git-ignored. Inline comments explain why, not what. Errors actionable; graceful degradation. No secrets in source.

Rules:
- **Never commit `.env` or `servicebus/Config.json`** — both contain local configuration and are git-ignored.
- Passwords: min 8 characters, mixed case, digit, special character.
- `servicebus` starts only after `servicebus-sql` is healthy.
- Volumes persist; only `.\stack.ps1 nuke` or `docker compose down -v` removes them.
- No CI/CD pipelines; no automated test suite, unit or integration tests.
- PowerShell 5.1+ compatibility — do not introduce syntax that requires PowerShell 7+ (e.g. ternary operators, null-coalescing, pipeline chain operators, multi-argument `Join-Path`).
- Keep `.env.example` and `Config.example.json` in sync — new `docker-compose.yml` variables go in `.env.example` and `README.md`; Service Bus entity changes go in `Config.example.json`.

Troubleshooting: unhealthy: check password complexity and `.\stack.ps1 logs <service>`; ports: edit `.env`, restart; timeout >120 s: `.\stack.ps1 pull`, check Docker limits; SQL: ensure `TrustServerCertificate=True`; Service Bus: verify `servicebus-sql` healthy and check logs.
